title: Ledgers (records files other than events, proposals and decisions; one JSON object per line)
description: Each ledger file holds one kind of record. All are append-only. A change of status is a new line that refers to the earlier one. Which file uses which definition is given in x-files. Every definition adds its fields to the common record fields (common.schema.json).

signature.description: Core. The founder's signature on a decision, or refusal to sign it, given at close-out. Written only by scripts/fos_close.py (captured_by close_script), never by a member.

decision_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the decision's line exactly as written. If the line ever changed, the signature no longer matches it.

answer.description: signed: final. refused: not signed; the decision stays a proposal. sent_back: returned to the members with the founder's note, to be reworked and asked again as a new decision.

mode.description: terminal: answered by a person at a terminal. test: the seed's self-test; never counts in a real organization.

note.description: The founder's note, given with a signature or when sending a decision back.

shown.description: What the founder was shown before answering: the decision's effects (what signing makes part of the organization), its warnings, the check result, the files changed since the last close-out, and whether it was asked on its own or in the routine group.

founding.description: Present on the founding only: the word the founder typed at the close-out's prompt, Found the organization now on this charter? (type FOUND). It alone founds the organization. The close-out commits this signature on its own ([FOUND]) before any structure, and the check and the witness read the founding from that commit.

shown_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact text the founder was shown for this decision, so the signature traces to what was reviewed.

decline.description: Core. Something stopped or turned back (by a rule, a check, the founder or a member): the visible trace of structure acting on the work.

by.description: Who applied the rule (role instance or founder).

rule_id.description: The rule or check that declined it, e.g. CORE-13 or a check ID.

what.description: What was proposed or drafted, briefly.

enforced_by.description: Optional. When an enforcement add-on in the agent app refused the write: its tool ID in org/TOOLS.json (docs/ENFORCEMENT.md).

correction.description: memory module. Something in the organization's work or conduct that was wrong, and the structural fix. (A wrongly written record is corrected by a record_correction event instead.)

caught_by.description: Who caught it: founder, a role instance, a check ID, or an outside reader.

escaped.description: True if it had already left the folder before it was caught.

failure_class.description: A class from modules/design-ahead/MODULE.md, or other.

structural_fix.description: The change to structure that should prevent a repeat, as a proposal ID, or none yet.

claim.description: Core (CORE-13), fuller with the claim-discipline module. A claim matched to its source at the moment the source is used, or marked lead.
The sentence as we use it.

cites.description: The citation as it appears in the work: a URL, DOI, arXiv ID, ISBN, or author and year.

source_file.description: Path under sources/. Empty only if status is lead or unable.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the saved source when the claim was recorded; fos_log fills it. If the file is later replaced, the check says so.

quote.description: Exact supporting words from the source.

finding_or_ours.description: finding: the source says it. ours: our inference from it.

scope.description: The limits the source places on it: population, measure, conditions.

about_member.description: True when the claim is about how a member or a model behaves.

runs.description: For a claim about a member's behaviour: how many runs or observations it rests on.

evidence.description: For a claim about a member's behaviour: how far the runs behind it reach.

commitment.description: memory module. A promise of future work, with its owner and what starts it.

id.description: K-0001 ... A later line with the same id records a new state.

trigger.description: What starts it: a date, an event, a decision.

recall.description: memory module. A cold-recall check at the start of a session (onboarding/SECOND_SESSION.md).

dissent.description: norms module. A member says a rule seems wrong for a case.

response.description: What happened: a decision ID, or noted.

review.description: review module. One run of a check held by a role.

object.description: What was checked: a file path or work item.

unique_catch.description: True when this review found something no other check or reader found; kept so that checks are kept or retired on what only they catch.

need.description: tool-making module. A need noticed. A need closed by hand or by a tool the organization already has counts as progress.

id.description: N-0001 ... A later line with the same id records a new state.

recurs.description: How often the task comes up.

cost_now.description: What doing it now costs, in time or effort.

drill.description: Core. A drill the founder plants to test whether a check or a member catches a known fault. Written only by scripts/fos_drill.py (captured_by drill_script). At planting, only a fingerprint (seal) of the founder's description is recorded; the description itself stays outside the folder until the founder reveals it.

id.description: DR-0001 ... The reveal is a later line with the same id.

seal.description: planted: SHA-256 of salt + description, in hex.

announced.description: planted: whether members were told that a drill is under way.

hint.description: planted, optional: what members were told (for example, a folder).

description.description: revealed: the founder's description of the planted fault.

salt.description: revealed: the salt used in the seal.

outcome.description: revealed: whether the fault was caught.

caught_by.description: revealed and caught: the role instance or check (for example CK-1) that caught it. Left out when the drill was missed: a miss is recorded as outcome missed, with no catcher.

pin.description: memory module. Something the founder chose to come back to later, in the founder's own words, with what should bring it back. Read at every roll-call; a later line with the same id records a new state.

words.description: What the founder said, word for word.

trigger.description: What should bring it back: a date, an event, a session count, a decision.

outcome.description: When revisited or dropped: what happened, or the decision ID.

deviation.description: design-ahead module, and every study. A change made after the design was frozen (a study's plan, or a design the founder declared fixed), with its kind, so that later readers can tell a forced change from a chosen one.

class.description: forced: imposed from outside (for example, a producer retired or changed a model); correction: an error in the design or its use was fixed; discretionary: chosen.

forced_by.description: For a forced change: what forced it.

outcome_seen.description: Whether any results the change could bear on had been seen before it was made.

expected_effect.description: What the change may do to the results, and in which direction, as far as anyone can say.

success.description: norms module. Something that went well, kept as an example to learn from, beside what was turned back and what was corrected.

evidence.description: Where it shows in the record: record IDs, files, commits.

by.description: Who did it (role instance or founder).

lesson.description: What to keep doing, in one sentence.
